records.source: οἱ κύριοι, τὸ δίκαιον καὶ τὴν ἰσότητα τοῖς δούλοις παρέχεσθε, εἰδότες ὅτι καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔχετε κύριον ἐν οὐρανῷ.
records.gloss: The masters, the just and the fairness to the slaves grant, knowing that also you have a Master in heaven.
pieces: Masters, give your slaves what is right and fair, because you know that you too have a Master in heaven.

L.1: Masters, grant your slaves what is just and fair, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.

R.1: Masters, treat your slaves in a way that is right and fair. Remember that you also have a Master, the Lord in heaven.

decisions.choice: what is just and fair: what is right, and what treats them as equals before God
decisions.reason: δίκαιον is what is just; ἰσότητα means equality or fairness. Masters owe their slaves more than the law demanded: fair treatment, as people who stand on the same level before the one Lord (3:11, 3:25).

decisions.choice: masters, and a Master in heaven: Christ, the Lord of masters and slaves alike
decisions.reason: The same word, κύριος, names the masters and their Master. They are answerable to Christ just as their slaves are (3:22-24; Ephesians 6:9).

decisions.choice: this verse completes the words to slaves and masters
decisions.reason: The chapter division falls in the middle of the household rules; this verse belongs with 3:22-25.

decisions.choice: masters; a Master in heaven
decisions.reason: "Masters" for the owners, as in 3:22, and "Master" with a capital for Christ, to keep the play on the one Greek word (m2). Readable adds "the Lord" so the reader knows who is meant.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as in 3:22: Paul speaks to owners about people they actually owned (m2, m3), and "servant" would change the meaning for modern readers (style guide).

records.source: Τῇ προσευχῇ προσκαρτερεῖτε, γρηγοροῦντες ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν εὐχαριστίᾳ, προσευχόμενοι ἅμα καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν, ἵνα ὁ θεὸς ἀνοίξῃ ἡμῖν θύραν τοῦ λόγου, λαλῆσαι τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι’ ὃ καὶ δέδεμαι, ἵνα φανερώσω αὐτὸ ὡς δεῖ με λαλῆσαι.
records.gloss: In the prayer persist, keeping alert in it with thanksgiving, \v 3 praying at the same time also for us, that the God may open to us a door of the word, to speak the mystery of the Christ, because of which also I have been bound, \v 4 so that I may make it clear as it is necessary for me to speak.
pieces: Keep on praying, and stay alert as you pray, giving thanks.
Pray for us too, that God will open a door for our message, so that we can tell the mystery of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, which is why I am in chains.
Pray that I may make it clear, as I ought to.

L.2: Persist in prayer, keeping alert in it with thanksgiving,
L.3: praying at the same time for us also, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, for which I am also bound,
L.4: so that I may make it clear, as I must speak.

R.2: Never stop praying. Stay awake and alert when you pray, and always thank God.
R.3: Pray for us too. Ask God to give us a chance to tell people the message, the mystery about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} that God has now made known. It is because I told this message that I am a prisoner now.
R.4: Pray that I will explain it clearly, the way I should.

decisions.choice: persist: keep at it, refuse to give up
decisions.reason: προσκαρτερέω means to hold fast to something and keep at it, as the first believers did in prayer (Acts 1:14; 2:42).

decisions.choice: keeping alert: awake and watchful
decisions.reason: γρηγορέω means to stay awake. Jesus told his disciples to keep awake and pray (Mark 14:38), and the word also points to watching for his coming (1 Thessalonians 5:6).

decisions.choice: open a door for the word: give an opportunity to preach
decisions.reason: An open door is a picture for an opportunity God gives to speak the gospel (1 Corinthians 16:9; 2 Corinthians 2:12). Paul asks for that, not first for his release.

decisions.choice: us: Paul and his fellow workers
decisions.reason: Paul asks prayer for "us", his whole team, then speaks of himself: "I am bound", "I may make it clear".

decisions.choice: I am bound: Paul writes as a prisoner
decisions.reason: δέδεμαι means to be bound or in chains. Paul is in custody because of the gospel (4:10, 4:18; compare Philippians 1:13 and Ephesians 6:20). The letter does not say where he was held.

decisions.choice: so that I may make it clear: the purpose of the open door
alternatives: a second request, alongside the first
decisions.reason: ἵνα φανερώσω says what Paul wants to do with the opportunity: make the mystery plain, "as I must", the task given him (1:25-27).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: give us a chance to tell people the message, the mystery about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} that God has now made known
alternatives: open a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ
decisions.reason: Readable explains the open door (m3) and recalls what the mystery is (1:26-27).

decisions.choice: Pray that I may make it clear (B); Pray that I will explain it clearly (R)
alternatives: so that I may make it clear
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start a new sentence and repeat "pray" so the request is plain.

records.heading: Pray, and live wisely with outsiders

records.source: Ἐν σοφίᾳ περιπατεῖτε πρὸς τοὺς ἔξω, τὸν καιρὸν ἐξαγοραζόμενοι.
records.gloss: In wisdom walk toward those outside, the time buying up.
pieces: Live wisely with those outside the church, making the most of every opportunity.

L.5: Walk in wisdom toward those outside, buying up the time.

R.5: Be wise in the way you live with people who are not believers. Use every chance you get to do good.

decisions.choice: those outside: people who are not believers
decisions.reason: "Those outside" is a common way of speaking of people outside the church (1 Corinthians 5:12-13; 1 Thessalonians 4:12). How believers live is seen by them.

decisions.choice: buying up the time: making the most of each opportunity
decisions.reason: ἐξαγοράζω means to buy up, to buy out. With καιρὸν, the right or opportune time, it means seizing every opening (Ephesians 5:16). In Daniel 2:8 the same phrase means trying to gain time, but that sense does not fit here.

decisions.choice: Live (B); Be wise in the way you live (R)
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a figure for how one lives; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: outside the church; making the most of every opportunity (B); people who are not believers; every chance you get to do good (R)
alternatives: those outside; buying up the time
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "those outside" are and what the idiom means (m1, m2). Readable's "to do good" names what the opportunity is for.

records.source: ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν πάντοτε ἐν χάριτι, ἅλατι ἠρτυμένος, εἰδέναι πῶς δεῖ ὑμᾶς ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ ἀποκρίνεσθαι.
records.gloss: The word of you always in grace, with salt seasoned, to know how it is necessary for you each one to answer.
pieces: Let your conversation always be gracious and seasoned with salt, so that you know how to answer each person.

L.6: [Let] your speech [be] always with graciousness, seasoned with salt, so that you know how you ought to answer each one.

R.6: Always speak in a kind and pleasant way, and make what you say interesting, like food with salt in it. Then you will know how to give a good answer to anyone who asks you something.

decisions.choice: with grace: gracious, pleasing and kind
decisions.reason: χάριτι is the word for grace, but in speech it means what is gracious and pleasing, as in Luke 4:22, where people wonder at Jesus' "gracious words". Kind speech also reflects the grace they have received.

decisions.choice: seasoned with salt: lively and worth hearing
decisions.reason: Greek writers spoke of witty, lively talk as salted. Salt also kept food from spoiling, and some take it as speech free from what is rotten (compare 3:8); the main idea is speech with flavor, not dull or bland.

decisions.choice: to know how to answer each one: speech that fits the person
decisions.reason: ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ ("each one") means every individual: the right answer depends on who is asking (1 Peter 3:15).

decisions.choice: graciousness (L); gracious (B); kind and pleasant (R)
decisions.reason: The sense here is gracious speech (m1), so the key term "grace" is not used.

decisions.choice: [Let] ... [be]
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb.

decisions.choice: make what you say interesting, like food with salt in it
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m2).

records.source: Τὰ κατ’ ἐμὲ πάντα γνωρίσει ὑμῖν Τυχικὸς ὁ ἀγαπητὸς ἀδελφὸς καὶ πιστὸς διάκονος καὶ σύνδουλος ἐν κυρίῳ, ὃν ἔπεμψα πρὸς ὑμᾶς εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἵνα γνῶτε τὰ περὶ ἡμῶν καὶ παρακαλέσῃ τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν, σὺν Ὀνησίμῳ τῷ πιστῷ καὶ ἀγαπητῷ ἀδελφῷ, ὅς ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν· πάντα ὑμῖν γνωρίσουσιν τὰ ὧδε.
records.gloss: The things concerning me all will make known to you Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant and fellow slave in [the] Lord, \v 8 whom I sent to you for this very [purpose], that you may know the things concerning us and he may encourage the hearts of you, \v 9 with Onesimus the faithful and beloved brother, who is of you; all things to you they will make known, the [things] here.
pieces: Tychicus will tell you all my news. He is a dear brother, a faithful servant and a fellow slave in the Lord.
I am sending him to you for this very reason, so that you may know how we are and so that he may encourage your hearts.
He is coming with Onesimus, our faithful and dear brother, who is one of your own. They will tell you everything that is happening here.

L.7: Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant and fellow slave in [the] Lord, will make known to you all the things concerning me.
L.8: I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that you may know the things concerning us and that he may encourage your hearts,
L.9: with Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you all the things here.

R.7: Tychicus will tell you all about how I am doing. He is a brother we love. He serves the Lord faithfully, and he is a slave of the Lord, as we are.
R.8: That is why I am sending him to you. I want you to know how we are, and I want him to encourage you.
R.9: Onesimus is coming with him. He is a faithful brother whom we love, and he is from your own town. They will tell you everything that is happening here.

decisions.choice: Tychicus: one of Paul's companions from the province of Asia, who carried the letter
decisions.reason: Tychicus was from Asia (Acts 20:4) and is also named as Paul's messenger in Ephesians 6:21-22. "I have sent" is written from the readers' point of view: when they read the letter, he will have arrived with it.

decisions.choice: servant and fellow slave: one who serves, and one who belongs to the same Master
decisions.reason: διάκονος is the word used of Epaphras and of Paul (1:7, 1:23, 1:25). σύνδουλος is the word for "fellow slave" used of Epaphras in 1:7: Tychicus, like Paul, belongs to Christ.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "that you may know the things concerning us"
alternatives: "that he may know the things concerning you"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "that he may know about you". The two readings differ by a few letters in Greek. The SBLGNT's reading matches what Paul says in verses 7 and 9, that Tychicus comes to tell them Paul's news. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: I have sent: the past tense of letters
decisions.reason: ἔπεμψα is past, written from the time the letter will be read, though Tychicus is carrying it. Balanced and Readable say "I am sending".

decisions.choice: Onesimus: a Colossian, very likely the slave for whom Paul wrote to Philemon
decisions.reason: Paul's letter to Philemon asks him to welcome back his slave Onesimus, who has become a believer, "no longer as a slave, but more than a slave, a dear brother" (Philemon 10-16). Archippus is named in both letters (verse 17; Philemon 2), so the two letters were most likely sent together. Here Paul calls Onesimus simply "the faithful and beloved brother".

decisions.choice: one of you: from Colossae
decisions.reason: The same words are used of Epaphras in verse 12.

decisions.choice: fellow slave (L, B); a slave of the Lord, as we are (R)
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level: "servant" already renders the other word in this sentence ("a faithful servant"), and the style guide keeps the two words apart (m2).

decisions.choice: I am sending
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the tense natural in English (m4).

decisions.choice: the sentence is divided
decisions.reason: The Greek is one sentence, which ends with a raised dot inside verse 9. Every level divides it so that the people named are easy to follow.

records.heading: News and greetings

records.source: Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Ἀρίσταρχος ὁ συναιχμάλωτός μου, καὶ Μᾶρκος ὁ ἀνεψιὸς Βαρναβᾶ περὶ οὗ ἐλάβετε ἐντολάς, ἐὰν ἔλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς δέξασθε αὐτόν, καὶ Ἰησοῦς ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰοῦστος, οἱ ὄντες ἐκ περιτομῆς, οὗτοι μόνοι συνεργοὶ εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, οἵτινες ἐγενήθησάν μοι παρηγορία.
records.gloss: Greets you Aristarchus the fellow prisoner of me, and Mark the cousin of Barnabas, concerning whom you received instructions, if he comes to you, receive him, \v 11 and Jesus the [one] called Justus, the [ones] being of [the] circumcision, these only fellow workers for the kingdom of the God, who have become to me a comfort.
pieces: Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, sends you greetings, and so does Mark, the cousin of Barnabas. You have had instructions about him: if he comes to you, make him welcome.
Jesus who is called Justus greets you too. Of all the Jewish believers, these are the only ones working with me for the kingdom of God, and they have been a great comfort to me.

L.10: Aristarchus my fellow prisoner greets you, and Mark the cousin of Barnabas (concerning whom you received instructions: if he comes to you, welcome him),
L.11: and Jesus who is called Justus. These, of those of the circumcision, [are the] only fellow workers for the kingdom of God, [and they] have been a comfort to me.

R.10: Aristarchus, who is in prison with me, says hello. So does Mark, the cousin of Barnabas. You have already been told what to do about Mark: if he comes to you, welcome him.
R.11: Jesus, who is also called Justus, says hello too. These three are the only Jewish believers who are working with me to spread the news of God's kingdom. They have been a great comfort to me.

decisions.choice: Aristarchus: a Macedonian from Thessalonica who traveled with Paul
decisions.reason: Aristarchus was with Paul at Ephesus and on the voyage to Rome (Acts 19:29; 20:4; 27:2), and is named in Philemon 24.

decisions.choice: fellow prisoner: sharing Paul's captivity
alternatives: a fellow soldier, 'captured' by Christ (a figure of speech)
decisions.reason: συναιχμάλωτός means a fellow captive, at first a prisoner of war. Aristarchus may have shared Paul's imprisonment, or chosen to stay with him; in Philemon 23 the same word is used of Epaphras.

decisions.choice: Mark, the cousin of Barnabas
decisions.reason: John Mark left Paul and Barnabas partway through their first journey, and Paul later refused to take him again, which parted Paul and Barnabas (Acts 13:13; 15:37-39). Here he is back among Paul's fellow workers (Philemon 24; compare 2 Timothy 4:11).

decisions.choice: the instructions: earlier word about Mark, and now "welcome him"
decisions.reason: The Colossians had already been told about Mark in some way the letter does not explain. The words "if he comes to you, welcome him" may be those instructions, or Paul's own request now.

decisions.choice: the only Jewish believers among Paul's fellow workers
alternatives: these are the only ones who are Jews
decisions.reason: οἱ ὄντες ἐκ περιτομῆς ("those of the circumcision") are Jewish believers. Paul means that of the Jewish believers, only these three are working with him where he is; the other fellow workers named next are Gentiles.

decisions.choice: comfort: encouragement and relief
decisions.reason: παρηγορία is found only here in the New Testament. It means comfort, relief, consolation.

decisions.choice: Balanced and Readable say "greets you" for each name and split the sentence
decisions.reason: The Greek has one verb for three people; repeating it keeps the list clear.

decisions.choice: says hello
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for a greeting.

records.source: ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Ἐπαφρᾶς ὁ ἐξ ὑμῶν, δοῦλος Χριστοῦ, πάντοτε ἀγωνιζόμενος ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐν ταῖς προσευχαῖς, ἵνα σταθῆτε τέλειοι καὶ πεπληροφορημένοι ἐν παντὶ θελήματι τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: Greets you Epaphras the [one] of you, a slave of Christ, always struggling on behalf of you in the prayers, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in all [the] will of the God.
pieces: Epaphras, one of your own and a servant of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, sends you greetings. He always wrestles for you in his prayers, asking that you will stand firm, mature and fully sure of everything God wills.

L.12: Epaphras, who is one of you, a slave of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, greets you, always struggling for you in [his] prayers, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in all the will of God.

R.12: Epaphras, who is from your town, says hello. He is a servant of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He always prays hard for you. He asks God to help you stand strong, grown up in your faith and completely sure of all that God wants.

decisions.choice: a slave of Christ: one who belongs to Christ
decisions.reason: δοῦλος is the title Paul gives himself and Timothy in Philippians 1:1. Epaphras is wholly Christ's, as 1:7 has already said ("our fellow slave").

decisions.choice: struggling: hard effort, like an athlete's
decisions.reason: ἀγωνίζομαι is the verb of 1:29, from the word for the contest in 2:1. Epaphras's struggle for them is in prayer.

decisions.choice: stand mature and fully assured in all the will of God
alternatives: stand ... filled with all the will of God
decisions.reason: τέλειοι is the "mature" of 1:28. πεπληροφορημένοι means fully convinced, sure (Romans 4:21). Many manuscripts read a word meaning "filled" instead; the meaning is close. They are to know God's will and be sure of it (1:9).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "a slave of Christ"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "Christ Jesus". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: wrestles
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of physical effort (m2).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that Epaphras belongs to Christ, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτῷ ὅτι ἔχει πολὺν πόνον ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν ἐν Λαοδικείᾳ καὶ τῶν ἐν Ἱεραπόλει.
records.gloss: I bear witness for to him that he has much toil on behalf of you and of those in Laodicea and of those in Hierapolis.
pieces: I can vouch for him that he works hard for you and for the believers in Laodicea and Hierapolis.

L.13: For I bear witness for him that he has much toil for you and for those in Laodicea and for those in Hierapolis.

R.13: I can tell you that he works very hard for you and for the believers in the towns of Laodicea and Hierapolis.

decisions.choice: toil: hard, painful labor
decisions.reason: πόνον is labor that costs effort and pain. Many manuscripts have a different word, "zeal", which may be a copyist's replacement for an unusual word; the SBLGNT has πόνον.

decisions.choice: Laodicea and Hierapolis: the neighboring towns of the Lycus valley
decisions.reason: Laodicea lay about ten miles from Colossae (2:1), and Hierapolis a few miles north of Laodicea. Epaphras seems to have brought the gospel to all three towns (1:7).

decisions.choice: the believers in Laodicea and Hierapolis
alternatives: those in Laodicea and those in Hierapolis
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "those in" these towns are: the churches there.

records.source: ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Λουκᾶς ὁ ἰατρὸς ὁ ἀγαπητὸς καὶ Δημᾶς.
records.gloss: Greets you Luke the physician the beloved, and Demas.
pieces: Our dear friend Luke, the doctor, sends you greetings, and so does Demas.

L.14: Luke the beloved physician greets you, and Demas.

R.14: Luke, the doctor, whom we love, says hello. So does Demas.

decisions.choice: Luke the physician
decisions.reason: Luke is named among Paul's fellow workers in Philemon 24 and 2 Timothy 4:11. Only here are we told he was a doctor. Early church tradition names him as the author of the Gospel of Luke and Acts.

decisions.choice: Demas
decisions.reason: Demas is one of Paul's fellow workers in Philemon 24. 2 Timothy 4:10 later says he left Paul, "having loved this present world".

decisions.choice: the doctor
decisions.reason: Everyday English.

records.source: ἀσπάσασθε τοὺς ἐν Λαοδικείᾳ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ Νύμφαν καὶ τὴν κατ’ οἶκον αὐτῆς ἐκκλησίαν.
records.gloss: Greet the in Laodicea brothers and Nympha and the in [the] house of her church.
pieces: Give my greetings to the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in Laodicea, and to Nympha and the church that meets in her house.

L.15: Greet the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in Laodicea, and Nympha and the church in her house.

R.15: Say hello for me to the believers in Laodicea. Also say hello to Nympha and to the church that meets in her home.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "Nympha and the church in her house"
alternatives: "Nymphas and the church in his house"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ over whether this person is a woman, Nympha ("her house"), or a man, Nymphas ("his house"); some read "their house". The name's form in Greek can be either. The SBLGNT reads "her", found in some important early manuscripts; a copyist might more easily have changed a woman's name to a man's than the reverse.

decisions.choice: the church in her house: a congregation that met in a home
decisions.reason: The first churches met in houses, often of a believer who had room and means (Romans 16:5; Philemon 2). Nympha was the host, and perhaps the leader, of such a church, probably in Laodicea or near it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The church in Laodicea included women and men. Readable says "the believers", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: the church that meets in her house
decisions.reason: The church is the people, not the building; "meets" says so.

records.source: καὶ ὅταν ἀναγνωσθῇ παρ’ ὑμῖν ἡ ἐπιστολή, ποιήσατε ἵνα καὶ ἐν τῇ Λαοδικέων ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀναγνωσθῇ, καὶ τὴν ἐκ Λαοδικείας ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀναγνῶτε.
records.gloss: And when is read among you the letter, cause that also in the of [the] Laodiceans church it is read, and the [one] from Laodicea that also you read.
pieces: When this letter has been read to you, see that it is also read in the church at Laodicea, and that you in turn read the letter that comes from Laodicea.

L.16: And when the letter has been read among you, see that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you also read the [letter] from Laodicea.

R.16: After you read this letter, send it to the church in Laodicea so they can read it too. And make sure you read the letter that is coming to you from Laodicea.

decisions.choice: read: read aloud to the gathered church
decisions.reason: ἀναγινώσκω means read, and letters were read aloud to the assembly (1 Thessalonians 5:27). Most believers heard Paul's letters rather than reading them.

decisions.choice: the letter from Laodicea: a letter we do not have
decisions.reason: This is most likely a letter of Paul's sent to Laodicea, to be passed on to Colossae. It has not survived, unless it is a letter we know by another name: some think of Ephesians, which may have gone to several churches, and some of Philemon. The letter does not say, so no identification is certain.

decisions.choice: send it to the church in Laodicea
alternatives: see that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans
decisions.reason: Readable says how the letter would be read there: by sending it on.

records.source: καὶ εἴπατε Ἀρχίππῳ· Βλέπε τὴν διακονίαν ἣν παρέλαβες ἐν κυρίῳ, ἵνα αὐτὴν πληροῖς.
records.gloss: And say to Archippus: See to the ministry which you received in [the] Lord, that it you may fulfill.
pieces: And tell Archippus, "Make sure you carry out fully the ministry you received in the Lord."

L.17: And say to Archippus, "See to the ministry that you received in [the] Lord, that you fulfill it."

R.17: And tell Archippus, "Be sure to finish the work the Lord gave you to do."

decisions.choice: Archippus: a member of the household church in Philemon's home
decisions.reason: Philemon 2 greets "Archippus our fellow soldier" with Philemon and Apphia and the church in their house. The letter does not say what his task was.

decisions.choice: the ministry received in the Lord: a work of service given him by the Lord
decisions.reason: διακονίαν means service of any kind, often service in the church (Acts 6:4; 2 Timothy 4:5). παραλαμβάνω is the verb used in 2:6 for receiving what is handed on. Paul tells the whole church to remind him, so his task concerned them.

decisions.choice: the work the Lord gave you to do
alternatives: the ministry you received in the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable puts "ministry" in plain words.

records.source: Ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου.
records.gloss: The greeting with the my [own] hand of Paul.
pieces: I, Paul, write this greeting in my own hand.

L.18: The greeting [is] in my own hand, Paul's.

R.18: I, Paul, am writing this greeting with my own hand.

decisions.choice: Paul signs the letter in his own hand
decisions.reason: Paul usually dictated his letters to someone who wrote them down (Romans 16:22), and then added a greeting in his own handwriting as a mark that the letter was his (1 Corinthians 16:21; Galatians 6:11; 2 Thessalonians 3:17).

pieces: Remember that I am in chains.

R.18: Remember me, because I am a prisoner.

decisions.choice: remember my chains: pray for me and keep faith with me in my imprisonment
decisions.reason: μνημονεύω is more than calling to mind: it is to remember someone in prayer and care (Hebrews 13:3). Paul's chains are for the gospel (verse 3).

pieces: Grace be with you.

R.18: May God's grace be with you.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "Amen" at the end
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "Amen", as copyists often did at the end of a book.

decisions.choice: the grace: God's grace, which the letter has spoken of
decisions.reason: The article points to the grace already named in the letter: God's grace in Christ (1:2, 1:6). Paul's letters close with a wish for it.

decisions.choice: May God's grace
decisions.reason: Readable makes the closing a prayer and says whose grace it is (m2).
